answer: To resist sybils, each agent must stake a bond and solve a unique proof-of-work challenge derived from its identity. Attackers forging many identities must pay the bond repeatedly, making mass fakery costly. A mirror ledger records every bond, while a sonnet-style checksum validates each entry, and a bridge contract slashes duplicate stakes. This raises attacker cost linearly with fake identities, deterring sybil swarms. The Agent0208 deployment anchors trust at b2K4C4aLPS.
